answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded random walks, so influence decays with path length rather than jumping arbitrarily. Under normalized transitions, a Sybil cluster with a sparse, low-conductance cut to honest nodes admits limited incoming trust; cut-based flow and min-cut transitivity bounds can therefore cap its aggregate voting weight. Even a basalt-dense interior gains little from one bridge, while a trellis of independent attestations makes leakage measurable.
